# Phoneme guide: latin group

<!-- Generated by tools/build_annotation_guides.py. Edit that file, not this one. -->

Every phoneme token of `mbfa-latin` (208 tokens: 204 phonemes, 3 special tokens and the model's internal blank). The web interface shows the same text when you hover a phoneme.

How to read the tables:

- **Sounds like** is an approximation. The example words are the real thing: they are the most frequent words containing the token in the FLEURS test sentences (dev split) of 36 languages (Afrikaans, Azerbaijani, Bosnian, Catalan, Czech, Welsh, Danish, German, English, Spanish, Estonian, Finnish, French, Irish, Galician, Hungarian, Indonesian, Icelandic, Italian, Luxembourgish, Lithuanian, Māori, Malay, Maltese, Norwegian, Dutch, Polish, Portuguese, Romanian, Slovak, Slovenian, Swedish, Swahili, Tagalog, Turkish, Uzbek), written in the G2P's own tokens, which is exactly what the aligner sees.
- **Used most in** gives the languages that use the token most, as a share of all the phonemes of that language.
- **Also used for**: IPA the G2P wrote that has no token of its own in this model, so it was mapped to this one.
- **Rare** tokens never appear in those sentences: they come from untrained languages (Basque, Albanian, Latin …) or are very rare.

Accent marks on vowels (á, à, â, ǎ …) are pitch accents from the dictionaries of Slovenian and Lithuanian. They are separate tokens, but their boundaries are placed like those of the plain vowel.

## Where boundaries go

Suggested conventions. Agree on them before annotating, so that every annotator places boundaries the same way.

- **Stops (p t k b d g …).** A stop starts where the closure starts: energy drops to a near-silent gap, and the formants of the vowel before it end. It ends after its burst (and after its aspiration, for ʰ tokens), where the next sound begins.
- **Vowels.** Start at the first regular glottal pulse with clear formants; end where the formants fade or the next consonant's closure or noise begins.
- **Fricatives (s ʃ f x …).** The span of the noise: start and end where the high-frequency noise starts and stops.
- **Nasals (m n ŋ …).** A steady, low murmur with weak upper formants. The edges are usually sudden changes in energy.
- **Glides, laterals, r (j w l ɹ …).** Edges are smooth formant transitions: put the boundary at the middle of the transition.
- **Diphthongs (a͡ɪ …).** One token for both parts: from the start of the first vowel to the end of the second. Do not split it.
- **Pauses.** Leave a short pause between words as a gap, or insert SIL where the speaker clearly stops.

## Diacritics

Marks added to a base symbol change it as follows.

| mark | name | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| ◌̃ | nasalised | air also flows through the nose (French “an”, Portuguese “não”) |
| ◌̯ | non-syllabic | the weak, glide-like half of a diphthong; it is not a syllable on its own |
| ◌̩ | syllabic | forms a syllable with no vowel, as the n of “button” |
| ◌̥ | voiceless | said without vocal-fold vibration, as if whispered |
| ◌̪ | dental | the tongue tip touches the upper teeth |
| ◌̠ | retracted | made a little further back in the mouth |
| ◌̝ | raised | a little closer (tongue higher) than the plain symbol |
| ◌̞ | lowered | a little more open; a lowered fricative is a smooth approximant with no friction |
| ◌̺ | apical | made with the very tip of the tongue |
| ◌̻ | laminal | made with the blade of the tongue, just behind the tip |
| ◌̆ | extra-short | a very short version of the vowel |
| ◌́ | accent ´ (high) | the G2P's dictionary marks a pitch accent or stress here |
| ◌̀ | accent ` (low) | the G2P's dictionary marks a pitch accent or stress here |
| ◌̂ | accent ˆ (falling) | the G2P's dictionary marks a falling pitch accent |
| ◌̌ | accent ˇ (rising) | the G2P's dictionary marks a rising pitch accent |
| ʲ | palatalised | said with the tongue body raised toward the palate: a y-like colour (“soft” consonants) |
| ʰ | aspirated | followed by a puff of breath before the vowel starts (English “top” has one, “stop” does not) |
| ʷ | labialised | said with rounded lips |
| ʼ | ejective | a pop made by the throat, with no breath from the lungs |
| ʱ | breathy-voiced | voiced, then released with a breathy, murmured puff (Hindi “bh”, “gh”) |
| ˤ | pharyngealised (emphatic) | said with the tongue root pulled back: a darker, “heavy” sound (Arabic ط, ص) |
| ◌̚ | unreleased | a final stop with no audible burst: the closure is held and the sound ends silently |
| ◌̈ | centralised | said closer to the centre of the mouth than the plain vowel |

## Special tokens

| token | meaning |
|---|---|
| `SIL` | **silence**. A pause: no speech. Use it for a pause the speaker makes inside a segment. |
| `noise` | **noise**. A non-speech sound: a breath, cough, laugh or click. |
| `<unk>` | **unknown**. The G2P wrote a sound this model has no token for. Keep its time span; the label cannot say what it is. |
